A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RSR research work. All 31 pages in each version, including Appendices A–G, are readable; text extraction and rendered-page comparison support a reliable comparison of equations, figures, tables, and results.

before.justification: v4 reports original distillation experiments across 55 teacher-student pairs, simulation results, correlation analyses, and trajectory/teacher selection experiments, with additional empirical results in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original results, including the distillation experiments in Table 1 and the ablations, selection experiments, and GPQA-Diamond evaluation in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The RSR definition, rank clipping, surprisal-weighted trajectory and dataset aggregation, and selection procedures are unchanged in Sections 3.4 and 5 and Appendix A.8.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same NuminaMath-derived training problems and evaluate AIME’24, AIME’25, AMC’23, MATH500, and GPQA-Diamond. The supplementary selection scenarios in Appendix E.3 are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the correlation, trajectory-selection, teacher-selection, and supplementary comparisons. The two newly cited general-domain selection papers are discussed in Section 6 but are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The training data construction, model configurations, budgets, Acc@4 evaluation, 33-to-1 trajectory selection, and 200-trajectory teacher-selection protocol match. The supplementary protocols, including the 55k No-Selection baseline, are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendices D–E retain the same clipping and weighting ablations, alternative metric analyses, token-level case study, correctness-filtering analysis, and reduced-candidate and reduced-teacher experiments.

E5.justification: Both disclose three independent teacher-generation runs and three fine-tuning seeds for trajectory selection, with identical averaging practices in Appendix A. No uncertainty-reporting or statistical testing procedure is added or removed.

E6.justification: Reported numerical and qualitative results match throughout the main text and appendices. Examples include RSR’s average Spearman correlation of 0.86 in Table 4, Qwen-3-14B’s RSR-selection math average of 78.6 in Table 6, and the RSR GPQA average of 40.4 in Table 16.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11, the Zipf-mixture simulation assumptions, RSR aggregation derivations, and Appendix C’s computational complexity analysis are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about informative alignment, RSR’s correlation with post-training performance, and its utility for trajectory and teacher selection.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, interpretations of experimental outcomes, and broader-applicability discussion are unchanged. Both retain the same limitations concerning candidate quality, deeper theoretical characterization, and cross-domain validation.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and timing information, evaluation prompts, and code/data access statements are unchanged. The added funding acknowledgement supplies no new technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 6 newly acknowledges general-domain precedents for student-specific data selection, citing Selective Reflection-Tuning and From Quantity to Quality as references 23–24. Existing references otherwise match after renumbering, making this a limited expansion of research positioning.

P1.justification: A short passage in Section 6 is rewritten, including clarification to 'teacher reasoning models.' v5 also adds acknowledgements thanking reviewers and identifying funding, and updates date/version text. The remaining narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–30 retain their designs, captions, and placement. The added acknowledgements block and bibliography entries cause limited page-layout reflow on pages 10–15.

improvement.justification: Section 6 now explicitly acknowledges student-specific selection in general-domain instruction tuning and supplies two relevant antecedent references, modestly improving attribution and research context. The scientific methods, evidence, conclusions, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall benefit is limited.
